question: Why did scanner Browse reopen the app and Batch Convert fail in the packaged build?
answer: The embedded scanner passes --run-script to WYSIWYG.exe for Browse dialogs; main.py had no handler so it booted a second app. Added a runpy dialog-runner branch to main.py. imageconvert_available also missed the <bundle>/WysiScan/imageconvert path used by the main build. Both fixed and rebuilt (1.15.3.18 app + Inno installer).

question: Does WYSIWYG ever use the standalone WysiScan.exe, and is Image Convert in the standalone now?
answer: No: dev runs scanner_server.py via Python, frozen re-launches WYSIWYG.exe --wysiscan and imports the bundled module; Image Convert runs as WYSIWYG.exe --imageconvert; installer ships no WysiScan.exe. The standalone WysiScan.exe now bundles Image Convert (runtime files only, excluding .venvic) with -c and --imageconvert dispatch; verified /batch-convert success.

question: Why did clicking WysiScan open nothing in the packaged app but work in raw code?
answer: runWysiScan awaited /run-wysiscan before window.open; the endpoint now waits for the slow packaged scanner to boot, so Chrome expired the user gesture and blocked the popup. Fix: open the tab synchronously on click with a placeholder, then navigate to 127.0.0.1:8010 when the server reports success. Rebuilt app + installer.

question: How are flaws sharing a leading object grouped?
answer: groupFlaws runs groupLeadingObjects after adjective grouping: simple two-word flaws with the same first word merge the second word, e.g. 'sticker mark' + 'sticker residue' -> 'sticker mark/residue' (hyphen allowed). Only plain pairs participate; context/location/adjective grouping unaffected.

question: How does the Edit Conditions modal search work?
answer: Added #customOptionsSearch + clear button to the Edit Conditions modal; filters title/text for the selected category and media type. resetCustomOptionsSearchAndFocus clears the term, renders and focuses the input whenever the modal opens (Edit button and Edit List context menu).

question: What is the close button called in the Edit Conditions modal?
answer: The former Cancel button (cancelEditCustomOptionBtn) now reads 'Close'. Its behaviour is unchanged: cancels an in-progress edit first, otherwise closes the modal.

question: Why did clicking a filtered condition row edit the wrong item?
answer: The Edit Conditions list passed filtered display indexes into edit/delete/favourite, which re-filtered by media type, so search shifted the target by one (acted on the row below). Actions now pass the option object and resolve by identity: indexOf for edit/delete, direct mutation for favourite.

question: What was included in the 17:26 full rebuild?
answer: 1.15.3.18: WYSIWYG.exe (17:22, favorites stripped, .env/keys.txt copied into dist), standalone WysiScan.exe (17:23, 87.2MB with Image Convert), Inno installer (17:26, 487.2MB), set_password.exe unchanged. Changelog head v1.15.3.18.

question: Why did set_password.exe crash on another machine and how is it preserved?
answer: allpass.json there was empty/corrupt, causing a raw JSONDecodeError. The loader now tolerates UTF-8 BOM, warns and starts empty for blank files (backup kept), and exits cleanly with a message for invalid JSON. Installer ships dist_tools/set_password.exe with uninsneveruninstall so install/upgrade/uninstall never remove it.

question: Is set_password.exe shipped with the installer?
answer: No. It was briefly added then removed on request; the .iss has no InstallDelete/UninstallDelete entries and set_password is not in the file list, so a manually placed copy in C:\FYRTOOLS\WYSIWYG survives install/upgrade/uninstall. Installer rebuilt (487.2MB).

question: How should Promo Stamp/Promo Sticker on Booklet combine?
answer: Share the common leading word across prefixes in suffix grouping: 'Promo Stamp' + 'Promo Sticker' -> 'Promo Stamp/Sticker on Booklet' (mergeSharedPrefix in groupFlaws).

question: How do Digipak/Cardsleeve/Card Sleeve/Cardboard Sleeve packaging labels dedupe?
answer: When the sleeve-packaging term also appears in sleeveDesc or the sleeve multiselect, the sleevePkg label is replaced with 'Artwork' (same rule as Jcard/Sleeve -> Artwork), while flaw text keeps the term.

question: How should shared-adjective flaws with different contexts be joined?
answer: Hoist the shared adjective once, then join each subject with its own trailing context using '/': 'light wear to Booklet/Cellophane tearing', 'light scratching to Disc/spindle-wear'. A context shared by all subjects is still appended once; if all subjects share a leading subject word, only the differing context tails are slash-joined.

question: How should 'tearing to Box' + 'Sleeve tearing' combine?
answer: A shared-head pass (groupSharedHeads) runs after adjective grouping: a single-word head with a context ('tearing to Box') absorbs modifier-first items ending in the same head ('Sleeve tearing') -> 'tearing to Box/Sleeve'. Adjective-only modifiers (light, minor...) and multi-word heads are excluded.

question: Order of slash-joined objects in shared-head grouping?
answer: Objects keep the selection order of their source flaws: 'Cellophane tearing' + 'tearing to Box' -> 'tearing to Cellophane/Box'; 'tearing to Box' + 'Sleeve tearing' -> 'tearing to Box/Sleeve'.

question: Why did shared-head grouping miss 'Cellophane tearing' + 'tearing to Box'?
answer: The pass was position-dependent: it anchored on the first contexted flaw it reached and pushed any earlier modifier-first flaw out unmerged. Rewritten as a two-phase pass (build head groups from contexted flaws, then attach modifier-first flaws) so selection order no longer matters.

question: How to silence Qt DPI/monitor startup warnings?
answer: Set QT_LOGGING_RULES='qt.qpa.window.warning=false;qt.qpa.screen.warning=false' before importing PySide6 when running with --window; the warnings are benign (process already DPI-aware via python.exe manifest).

question: Should flaw grouping be case-insensitive?
answer: Yes. Prefix grouping, suffix grouping, shared-head grouping, adjective context matching and all slash-join de-dupes now compare case-insensitively via uniqueCI(), keeping the first spelling seen.

question: How do 'light Cellophane tearing' + 'Sleeve tearing' combine?
answer: New groupSuffixHeads pass (after groupSharedHeads): items sharing a trailing head word merge into one phrase and a single shared leading adjective is hoisted once -> 'light Cellophane/Sleeve tearing'. Skips items with to/through/on contexts and refuses to hoist when objects would be empty.

question: Why did 'light Cellophane tearing' + 'light Sleeve tearing' repeat 'tearing'?
answer: groupAdjectives joined the full remainders because splitFlaw returns the whole phrase when there is no context. The no-context branch now hoists a shared trailing head word: 'light Cellophane/Sleeve tearing'.

question: Should slash-expanded suffixes merge with plain suffixes?
answer: Yes. Suffix grouping now splits suffixes on '/' and merges subset/superset sets (case-insensitive), unioning components: 'Box' + 'Box/Sleeve' -> 'Box/Sleeve'. Also guards null suffixes that previously threw.

question: Which flaw locations are canonicalised?
answer: LOCATION_CANON now covers Corner, Edge, Ring and Spine (singular + plural), so 'Ring creasing' shares the flaw word with 'Corner creasing'.

question: Are hyphens grouping-agnostic?
answer: Yes for head/object parsing: splitWords() splits on whitespace and hyphens, so 'ring-wear' + 'shelf-wear' -> 'ring/shelf wear' (used by groupSuffixHeads and the no-context adjective branch). Context/adjective branch still preserves hyphens.

question: Hyphen-agnostic grouping scope?
answer: splitFlaw detects to/through/on case- and hyphen-insensitively; splitAdjective accepts hyphen separators; splitWords (whitespace+hyphen) used by splitHeadTail, groupAdjectives contexts, groupSharedHeads modifiers and mergeSharedPrefix. LOCATION_CANON stays whitespace-only so 'ring-wear' still reaches suffix-head grouping.

question: Can adjective-modified flaws join non-adjective flaws?
answer: No. groupSharedHeads now rejects a modifier-first flaw whose FIRST word is an intensity adjective, so 'light Cellophane tearing' stays separate from 'tearing to Booklet/Inlay'.

question: How are location-prefixed flaws grouped?
answer: canonicalizeLocations() turns 'Corner edge creasing' into 'Corner/Edge creasing'; groupSuffixHeads now also accepts location pseudo-separators (' ') so hyphen and space spellings group ('Edge creasing' + 'Spine-creasing' -> 'Edge/Spine creasing'); slash sets are flattened before unioning.

question: How are existing slash sets parsed when grouping heads?
answer: groupSuffixHeads.describe() now tokenises on '/', whitespace and hyphens and drops repeated head words, so 'Corner-creasing' + 'Corner creasing/Edge creasing' -> 'Corner/Edge creasing'.

question: Adjective+location flaws and hyphen preservation
answer: groupAdjectives branch 2 strips shared lead words from the original text so hyphens survive ('spindle-wear'); groupSuffixHeads keeps existing slash sets as separate objects. 'light Corner creasing' + 'light Edge creasing' -> 'light Corner/Edge creasing' (also hyphen spelling).

question: Does the noun-capitalisation rule apply to multiselect flaws?
answer: Yes. capitalizeFlawContext() is now applied to sleeve and media multiselect text/title values, matching the sleeve/media description text boxes.

question: Can media and sleeve flaws group together?
answer: No. Sleeve flaws appended to the media phrase are kept as an already-grouped list (sleeveFlawsForMedia) and only concatenated after groupFlaws(mediaEntries) runs, so cross-source grouping is impossible.

question: Are location nouns capitalised at the start of a flaw?
answer: Yes. capitalizeFlawContext() capitalises leading Corner/Edge/Ring/Spine (also behind an intensity adjective): 'corner denting' -> 'Corner denting', 'light corner-wear' -> 'light Corner-wear'.

question: Which prepositions capitalise their following noun?
answer: capitalizeFlawContext() capitalises the noun after to/through/on/at/near/around/along, preserving the original spacing or hyphen; 'X of Y' phrases and articles are still skipped.

question: All Types condition pickers: all columns active?
answer: Yes. The Media Type pull-down and its label were removed from #allTypesControls (only the Media/Sleeve view switch remains); all three column headers render blue and every column is clickable; Unfavorite All now clears all three types.

question: How can All Types columns toggle other media types?
answer: The inline #mediaConditionOptions / #sleeveConditionOptions selects now contain every media type's entries (non-current ones flagged option.hidden), so the All Types modal can toggle CD/LP/CASS rows while the main UI still lists only the current type; sleeve selections sync per type to lpOptions/cdOptions/customOptions.

question: Version bump for 2026-10-28 changes?
answer: Version 1.15.3.19 (version.json build 19 + wysiWyg-installer.iss) with a matching changelog header for the conditions/grouping/Digi-pak changes.

question: Does WYSIWYG use the standalone WysiScan.exe?
answer: No. main.py launches WysiScan/scanner_server.py with Python (resource_path) and has a --wysiscan branch importing WysiScan.scanner_server; the single-file WysiScan.exe is only for external tools (WysiChat launches C:\FYRTOOLS\WysiScan\WysiScan.exe). The installer now ships that exe to C:\FYRTOOLS\WysiScan.

question: Why does the Chrome context menu switch to 'Send to Amazon Add' only on /shop/item pages?
answer: Marketplace listing pages are the only ones the Amazon Adds scraper can fill from a live listing (price/location/comments via the marketplace API), so the page-level menu item is retitled via chrome.contextMenus.update() on tabs.onActivated/onUpdated and routed to Adds > Amazon. Other Discogs pages keep 'Send Page to WYSIWYG Scraper'.

question: Why open the Adds page at http://127.0.0.1:8008/adds/amazon?url=... instead of the file:// path?
answer: The page calls fetch('/api/adds/amazon-scrape') relatively, so a file:// open cannot reach the backend. The extension hands the listing URL off via a ?url= query param that the page reads on DOMContentLoaded, fills into #urlInput and auto-scrapes; the param is stripped with history.replaceState so a reload does not re-scrape. Clipboard is still written as a fallback.

question: How do client machines get extension updates if they load from the server share?
answer: Clients load the unpacked extension from \\server\FYRTOOLS\WYSIWYG\ChromeExt (server's installed copy, shared read-only by the .iss). background.js no longer compares against the app's /api/extension-version: it compares chrome.runtime.getManifest().version (what Chrome actually loaded) with version.json read from the extension folder with cache:no-store, and calls chrome.runtime.reload() on a mismatch. So a server-side file replace with a bumped version self-updates every client within 5 minutes; no manual reload.

question: Why does .section-title use scroll-margin-top: 52px?
answer: The section jump uses scrollIntoView({block:'start'}), which parks the title at viewport y=0 where the sticky #aapTopbar (~44px tall) covers it, so the heading looked like it was skipped. scroll-margin-top reserves the bar height plus a small gap so the title lands just under the bar.

question: Why does the Amazon Adds page open as a popup window from the context menu?
answer: chrome.windows.create({type:'popup', 820x860}) matches the shape the app's openAddsAmazon() uses with window.open, so the Adds page stays a small tool window rather than a browser tab. An already-open /adds/amazon tab or window is reused (tabs.update + windows.update focus) instead of opening duplicates.

question: Why does the Amazon Adds pin button call a local API instead of CSS?
answer: A web page cannot set its own OS window always-on-top, so the old in-page 'pin' only floated content inside the page (and its fixed wrapper covered the button, so it could not be unpinned). Now toggleAapPin() POSTs /api/window-pin {title: document.title, topmost}, and main.py finds the window by caption (exact match, then prefix to tolerate Chrome's ' - Google Chrome' suffix) and calls SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST/HWND_NOTOPMOST). The button keeps its place, flips glyph 📍/📌, and re-reads the real state on load via GET /api/window-pin.

question: How is the Amazon Adds pin state remembered between windows?
answer: localStorage key 'wysiwyg_adds_amazon_pin' ('1'/'0') is written on every successful toggle. The OS topmost flag dies with the window, so on DOMContentLoaded the page re-applies topmost=true via POST /api/window-pin when the stored value is '1' (silently, so it does not clobber the scrape status line); otherwise it just paints the state it reads from GET /api/window-pin.

question: Why was the Walmart Sheet removed from the GUI, installer and build?
answer: Walmart changed their upload items page so the sheet exporter no longer matches their format and the feature is retired. Removed the drawer button, hotkey/command-palette entry, runWalmartSheet(), clearWalmartCache(), the /api/walmart/cache-context auto-sync pushes, assembleWalmartDescription(), the Qt Tools > Walmart menu item, the walmart_router import/mount in main.py, plus the walmart.html / WalmartSheet --add-data flags and the .iss Source line. Source files (walmart.html, walmart.js, WalmartSheet/) are left on disk until explicitly deleted.

question: Why was the Amazon Adds Part Number (Cat#) truncated to the trailing digits?
answer: The label parser split the catalogue number on whitespace and kept only tokens containing digits, so 'ART CD 002' became '002' ('ART'/'CD' dropped). Fixed in Adds/Amazon_add_scraper.py: new split_cat_numbers() groups space-separated words into one number and only starts a new number when a self-contained token follows (has a letter prefix or digit-hyphen-digit, e.g. '314-526 542-4'), and the label name now comes from the dash-split pair instead of stripping digit tokens (which had left 'Odium Records - ART CD').

question: Why did the Amazon Adds page still open as a tab after the popup-window change?
answer: openAmazonAdd() reused any tab whose URL matched /adds/amazon, including one sitting in a normal tabbed window, so the page was navigated inside that tab. It now walks chrome.windows.getAll({populate:true}) and only reuses an Adds page that is already in a window of type 'popup'; otherwise it calls chrome.windows.create({type:'popup'}). Extension bumped to 1.5.

question: Why bump to v1.16.6.00 and log to docs/WORK_LOG.md now?
answer: This session's visible changes (extension context menu/popup, self-update hook, Amazon Adds pin, section jump, catalogue-number fix, Walmart removal) are release-worthy, so version.json and the .iss MyAppVersion moved 1.16.5.00 -> 1.16.6.00 with a matching changelog section. docs/CONVENTIONS.md requires every change in docs/WORK_LOG.md; entries 44-49 backfill that, plus new gotchas about reloading the extension and that Adds/ is bundled so page edits need a rebuild.

question: Why does the Amazon Adds page hide rows with display:none instead of re-rendering?
answer: The Hide Empty toggle must not lose edits typed into the field textareas, so applyHideEmpty() works on the already-rendered .field-row/.kw-group nodes and only flips display. Empty = blank, n/a/na/none/null/*(not found)*/need-sku/-/—, or any value containing 'check box:'; section headings with no visible rows are hidden too. Copy All skips rows hidden by the filter, and Copy All now flashes 'Copied' via flashCopied() like the per-row buttons.

question: Which Amazon Adds fields are hidden by Hide Empty regardless of content?
answer: Upload Photos and Merchant Shipping Group are hidden by label (EMPTY_LABELS in amazon_add_page.html) because their values are only Amazon form instructions ('(uploaded by user)', '(select correct weight by user)'), never data. Copy All therefore skips them too while the filter is on.

question: How does the Adds > Amazon 'Pull from WYSIWYG' button get the URL?
answer: Both pages are served from the same origin (http://127.0.0.1:8008), so app.js mirrors the Discogs URL box into localStorage['wysiwyg_last_discogs_url'] via rememberDiscogsUrl() on input and after click-to-autopaste (never overwriting with a blank), and the Adds page reads that key, fills #urlInput and scrapes. Avoids a server round-trip or scripting between windows.

question: Why does WysiScan's Extract Text run as its own browser window instead of a modal?
answer: The panel outgrew the in-page modal: it now opens via window.open('/?extract=1&files=[...]', 'WysiScanExtract') with no await before the call (so the click gesture survives). The same page reloads in extract mode - an inline script adds body.extract-mode before first paint, CSS hides every other body child and stretches #cliModal to the window, files travel in the URL and are held in cliFiles for submitCliPrompt(), the window sends its own /api/heartbeat so the 120s auto-shutdown cannot kill it, and Cancel/× close the window. Pin posts to a new scanner-side /api/window-pin (SetWindowPos HWND_TOPMOST) because a page cannot raise its own OS window.

question: Why did Re-Run in Extract Text not re-run, and how is it fixed?
answer: /run-cli-prompt returned the cached extraction whenever the file list matched, so the Re-Run label was cosmetic. Now the client sends force:true when the button is in Re-Run state (cliResultFromCache) or the prompt text changed (cliLastPromptSent - the cache key is files-only, so a new Custom prompt would otherwise return the old output), and the endpoint skips its cache lookup when force is set.

question: How does the Extract Text Discogs button build its marketplace search?
answer: searchDiscogsMarketplace() reads the rendered rows by label (cliFieldValue, using the textarea so manual edits count) and maps Band/Artist -> artist, Album Title -> release_title, Catalog Number -> catno on https://www.discogs.com/sell/list?sort=listed,desc&limit=250, opened in the named tab 'DiscogsMarketplaceSearch' so repeat searches reuse it. The 'Band Name' label was renamed to Band/Artist in prompts.json/default_prompt.json, and renderCliResults() normalises the old label so cached extractions show it too.

question: Why did the Extract Text Discogs button open an unfiltered marketplace page?
answer: The first version built /sell/list?artist=NAME&release_title=TITLE&catno=CATNO. Discogs moved the marketplace to /shop/list, whose search box takes a single free-text q (its per-field filters are internal IDs, so name-based params are dropped) - hence an unfiltered page. It now opens https://www.discogs.com/shop/list?q=Band/Artist+Album+Title, falling back to the catalogue number when artist/title are missing, and the button stays disabled until an extraction has produced fields (updateCliDiscogsBtn).

question: What goes into the Extract Text Discogs marketplace query?
answer: All extracted identifiers are folded into the single free-text q on https://www.discogs.com/shop/list: Band/Artist, Album Title, Catalog Number and UPC/Barcode (each included only when present), because the marketplace's per-field filters are internal IDs rather than names. cliDiscogsFields() is the single source for the query and for enabling/disabling the button.

question: Which Discogs marketplace URL does the Extract Text search open?
answer: https://www.discogs.com/sell/list?q=<Band/Artist Album Title Catalog# UPC> — the /sell marketplace search page the user prefers for picking a release to list against, not the redesigned /shop/list. Bare /sell is the seller hub with no result list, so the query goes on /sell/list.

question: How does the app tab get focus after the extension sends a URL to the scraper?
answer: ChromeExt/background.js calls focusAppTab() once POST /api/extension-scrape succeeds: findAppTab() picks the main-page tab (/, /index.html, /#… or /?… - not the Adds pages on the same host) then tabs.update({active:true}) + windows.update({focused:true}). Desktop(webview) mode needs nothing because main.py's scrape bridge already calls showNormal()/activateWindow()/raise_().

question: Why does the app reset before submitting a scrape?
answer: Every scrape path (manual button, Enter, SSE bridge, Chrome extension clicking #scrapeBtn) becomes a submit on form[hx-post=/scrape]. A document-level CAPTURE listener (so it beats htmx's element listener) prevents it, awaits fullReset(), restores #discogsUrlInput (fullReset clears all input[type=url]) and re-submits via requestSubmit() behind a guard flag - so leftover menus/SKU/description from the previous item can never land on the incoming scrape.

question: How is WysiChat built and deployed now?
answer: The root !build.bat gained a [3/3] step that builds WysiChat\\dist\\Wysichat.exe with PyInstaller onefile using the chat's own .venv (FreeSimpleGUI/cryptography), falling back to .venv311 then PATH python, run from inside WysiChat\\. It never wipes WysiChat\\dist because live chat_history_*.db / user_prefs_*.json sit there. wysiWyg-installer.iss now ships the exe + two pngs to C:\\FYRTOOLS\\WysiChat (same folder as the standalone chat installer, case-insensitive path), adds a Start Menu entry, a Defender exclusion and a taskkill of Wysichat.exe before install/uninstall; chat data files are never listed so upgrades cannot touch them.

question: What does the WYSIWYG installer put in C:\FYRTOOLS\WysiChat?
answer: Only Wysichat.exe. Both images are baked into the onefile exe via --add-data and read through resource_path(): fyrlogo_alert.png used to be loaded from the exe folder and is now bundled too, and create_alert_icon() swallows write failures so a read-only _MEIPASS cannot crash startup. Chat history (chat_history_<alias>.db), user_prefs_<alias>.json and logs live next to the exe and are never in the installer's file list, so upgrades replace just the exe and uninstall removes just the exe.

question: WysiChat tray menu and scanner wiring after the merge
answer: WysiChat's tray menu item 'Wysiscanner' was renamed to 'WysiScan' (label + tray_event handler) and launch_wysiscan() runs the standalone C:\\FYRTOOLS\\WysiScan\\WysiScan.exe (dev script fallback kept). The main app deliberately keeps using its bundled scanner via sys.executable --wysiscan and never launches WysiScan.exe. The build now deletes only WysiChat\\dist\\Wysichat.exe (never the folder, which holds live chat data) so a stale binary cannot mask a failed build; the installer overwrites that exe and removes only it on uninstall.

question: Standalone WysiScan.exe rebuild: what changed and the pytesseract gap
answer: Old WysiScan\\dist\\WysiScan.exe + WysiScan\\build were deleted and the scanner rebuilt with .venv311 -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --clean WysiScan.spec (83.2 MB); WysiScan\\dist also holds runtime scans/temp so only the exe and build dir were removed. scanner_test.html is bundled from source (sizes match). pytesseract is NOT installed in .venv311/.venv, so unlike the 28 Oct build the new exe omits it (warn-WysiScan.txt) - OCR paths fail gracefully and Tesseract is not installed here either; pip install pytesseract + rebuild would restore parity.

question: Is Tesseract/pytesseract used locally at all?
answer: No. Verified 13 Nov 2026: no tesseract.exe on PATH, Program Files, LOCALAPPDATA or the registry, no TESSDATA_PREFIX, and pytesseract is absent from .venv311, .venv and the embedded WysiWYG build (build\\WYSIWYG\\warn-WYSIWYG.txt lists it as missing, imported optionally by WysiScan.scanner_server and main.py). Logs confirm: 'Tesseract not available, skipping CD matrix orientation' on every CD scan, and an old March /ocr-and-lookup that logged TesseractNotFoundError. All calls are guarded, Extract Text uses Gemini, so builds intentionally omit pytesseract and the new WysiScan.exe matches the embedded behaviour.

question: How is 'Track Count' kept out of the listing HTML while the description text keeps it?
answer: The raw scrape text carries 'Track Count: N' and app.js parses it into #trackTimeInfo, which the description assembler turns into 'with N Tracks'. format_discogs_to_html() turned every 'Key: value' line into metadata, so it leaked into the HTML tab output - it now skips 'Track Count:'. Separately, Amazon generate_html_block() never showed a count but left its tracklist EMPTY for Discogs API positions ('1 Title', no dot) because start detection only matched A1 or '1.'; it now accepts ^\\d+\\s as well and recognises the 'Tracklist:' header (tracks start on the next line). html_format also strips a 'Tracklist:' header with the colon so it cannot render as a track.

question: Why was the HTML tab scratchpad removed and how do heights line up?
answer: The MANUAL INPUT / SCRATCHPAD box is gone (label, Copy All/Select All/Paste buttons, #manualInputBox), along with its listeners and helper functions; htmlGenBtn now sends #scraperResultText and main.py's scrape response just calls parsePastedData(rawText). No CSS change was needed for the height match: .details-grid is a fixed 600px grid and .details-box/.details-box-textarea are flex:1, so the single remaining box fills the column exactly like .preview-column's flex:1 preview. 'with N Tracks' is unaffected because the raw text still carries Track Count and parsePastedData still sets #trackTimeInfo (verified by running assembleDescription).

question: Why does a Gatefold sleeve condition now print 'Gatefold Sleeve'?
answer: With a sleeve condition chosen and the sleeve description box empty, the condition value sits in the sleeve-condition slot of assembleDescription, so 'Gatefold' rendered bare ('LP Vinyl Gatefold with ...'). The packaging slot already had a gatefold->'Gatefold Sleeve' rule in processFormatData but it required a sleeve description. assembleDescription now normalises the condition slot too (replace /gatefold(?!\\s*sleeve)/ig) but ONLY when fmtData.conditionPhrase is set, i.e. the blank-sleeve-description path - so the sleeve-description path is unchanged.

question: How does Scott test, and what restart info does he want after each change?
answer: He runs the SOURCE for all testing (python main.py / scanner from source) and never the built exe until changes are complete - so no rebuilds unless he asks. After every change he wants an explicit statement of what must be restarted: the app for any main.py or imported .py change (uvicorn has no reload), the scanner for scanner_server.py/scanner_test.html (HTML is cached in memory), a chrome://extensions reload for ChromeExt changes, or just Ctrl+F5 for HTML/JS served per request. Recorded in USER.md under 'How to work with them'.

question: Where is 'Gatefold Sleeve' enforced in the description?
answer: Two places in app.js: (1) assembleDescription normalises the sleeve-condition slot when fmtData.conditionPhrase is set (blank sleeve description), (2) processFormatData's packaging rule now runs regardless of sleeveDesc - the old '&& sleeveDesc' requirement caused the missing word for sleeve packaging Gatefold + multiselect flaws. Both use the /gatefold(?!\\s*sleeve)/ig lookahead so an existing 'Gatefold Sleeve' is never doubled; Digipak and the description-present path are untouched.

question: When does a Gatefold packaging print 'Sleeve'?
answer: Only when another sleeve attribute follows it: a sleeve condition, a sleeve description, or any sleeve multiselect flaw. sleeveHasContent = hasSleeveCondition || hasSleeveDesc || sleeveEntriesAll.length > 0 gates the gatefold -> 'Gatefold Sleeve' replacement in processFormatData. So a bare Gatefold prints '... LP Vinyl Gatefold is Out-of-Print ...' while 'Very Good Gatefold Sleeve with Corner creasing' keeps the noun. Lookahead (?!\\s*sleeve) prevents doubling; Digipak/no-packaging paths untouched.

question: How does the WysiScan Image Adjust panel work?
answer: New #adjust-ui panel below Tilt Correction (both wrapped in #left-controls). Five sliders preview live on #originalImg with CSS filters (brightness/contrast/saturate/hue-rotate) plus an inline SVG feComponentTransfer filter (#adjTintFilter, R/B intercept +v, G -v) for tint. Apply POSTs /adjust-image which snapshots a one-time <sanitized>.pristine into TEMP_DIR, creates an undo backup, applies numpy/OpenCV maths (contrast around mid-grey, brightness +/-1.28/step, HSV saturation+hue, tint R/B+ G-) and returns a cache-busted URL. Reset zeroes sliders only; Reset All POSTs /adjust-image-reset to restore the pristine file. Sliders are cleared on new scans/restores so previews cannot leak between images.

question: Does WysiScan Apply adjust both image copies?
answer: Yes - adjustTargetPaths() returns the original (originalImg.dataset.path / lastOriginalPath) and the cropped output (croppedImg.dataset.path / lastCroppedPath, skipped when identical), and applyImageAdjust() POSTs /adjust-image once per path so the Last Scan (Cropped) copy mirrors the previewed result. resetImageAdjustAll() walks the same two paths and restores each pristine snapshot (errors are counted, not spammed). refreshImageElements(path,url) updates the main view and thumbnails.

question: Which colours do the scanner's left-rail buttons use now?
answer: Apply (Tilt + Image Adjust) = Save green background-color:#28a745 with no colour override (inherits --btn-text, same as the Save buttons in the cropped row); Reset and Reset All = Full/Open blue (background: var(--btn-bg); color: var(--btn-text)); Auto-Align = Extract Text purple (#6f42c1, white text). Borders are 1px solid var(--accent-color), matching the generic button rule the reference buttons inherit.

question: How was the scanner's left rail compacted to remove scrolling?
answer: Removed the visible panel headings (Tilt Correction / Image Adjust), shortened button padding from 8px to 3px vertical (Auto-Align 5px), reduced the tilt number input padding, panel padding 15px->10px, panel gaps 10/8px->6/5px, #left-controls gap 20px->12px, and restyled the five range inputs to a 10px control (3px track, 10px thumb) via ::-webkit-slider-runnable-track/thumb. Roughly 150px of vertical space saved so the rail fits without scrolling.

question: Why did scanner code changes appear not to apply after a restart?
answer: /run-wysiscan returns 'already running' when port 8010 is in use, so clicking WysiScan re-uses the existing scanner process, and that process caches scanner_test.html in _INDEX_HTML_CACHE. App restarts do not help. The scanner process must be killed (taskkill /F /T on the scanner_server.py PIDs, or close its window and wait ~2 min for idle shutdown) before reopening. Verified 13 Nov 2026: running scanner started 10:13:46 while the edited file was written 10:19:34.

question: How do the install helpers close the app and its browser windows?
answer: kill_wysiwyg.bat and run_me_Installer.bat kill WYSIWYG/WysiScan/Wysichat plus a source-run scanner via a PowerShell command-line filter on Win32_Process (*scanner_server.py*), which leaves UberPaste and the main app's Python process alone (taskkill /IM cannot do that). They then run close_local_chrome.ps1, which EnumWindows-matches captions starting with WYSIWYG / WysiScan / 'Extract Text From Image(s)', requires the owner to be a browser, and posts WM_CLOSE - Chrome offers no external per-tab close, so the whole window showing that page is closed. timeout /t was replaced with ping waits because timeout fails without an interactive console.

question: What should Scott run between edits to close everything?
answer: kill-wysiwyg.ps1 (via the !powershell .kill-wysiwyg.ps1.bat wrapper) - it stops WYSIWYG.exe/WysiScan.exe/Wysichat.exe, a source-run scanner (*scanner_server.py*) AND a source-run app (*main.py*, command-line matched so UberPaste survives), closes local app browser windows via close_local_chrome.ps1, then waits for ports 8008/8010 to free. Supports -NoChrome, -WhatIf, -Quiet. kill_wysiwyg.bat / run_me_Installer.bat are install helpers: same exe + scanner kills and Chrome cleanup, but they do NOT stop 'python main.py'.

question: Which scripts close local Chrome windows?
answer: Only run_me_Installer.bat - it calls close_local_chrome.ps1 before installing. The dev helpers (kill-wysiwyg.ps1 and its .bat wrapper, and kill_wysiwyg.bat) deliberately leave browsers alone because closing a window takes the user's other tabs with it; they only stop WYSIWYG.exe/WysiScan.exe/Wysichat.exe plus source-run 'python main.py' and 'python scanner_server.py' processes, and the ps1 waits for ports 8008/8010 to free.

question: What are the scanner Crop Mode radios called now?
answer: CD Matrix (value cd), CD/45 Front (value tape) and Custom One (value lp) - only the visible labels changed. The value attributes stay cd/tape/lp because handleCropModeChange, paddingByMode and the scan/import media_type payloads key off the value, so behaviour is untouched.

question: How does CD/45 Front straighten scanned text?
answer: Two stages: (1) one small Gemini call (_ai_upright_degrees, image downscaled to 900px, prompt asks for ONLY 0/90/180/270 clockwise) for orientation - the only reliable way to distinguish upright from upside-down; (2) local levelling (_detect_text_skew) that rotates ±10deg candidates and keeps the one maximising the row-projection variance of the ink mask, refined to 0.25deg, ignoring sub-0.5deg corrections. Rotation uses _rotate_with_background (same math as /deskew-image) after create_backup so Undo works. Only media_type=='tape' is affected; auto/lp keep perform_auto_deskew and cd gets none. Verified 0/90/180 on synthetic images and within 0.25deg levelling.

question: Why does CD/45 Front check media_type == 'tape'?
answer: The radio's VALUE is 'tape' (legacy name from the cassette preset); only the visible label is 'CD/45 Front'. Comparing against 'cd' or '45' would never match (and 'cd' is the CD Matrix preset, which must not straighten). Renaming the values would also touch padding_by_mode keys persisted in config.json (auto/cd/tape/lp). Levelling also gained a >=10% improvement guard so a CD label face (curved/radial text, no horizontal rows) is never rotated on noise.

question: Why did a cmd window survive kill_wysiwyg.bat?
answer: Because it was not an app window: the main app prints PySide/Qt warnings and the scanner child (launched with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, sharing the parent console) prints Auto-cropping lines into the same console, whose title is the default 'C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\cmd.exe'. That is the cmd shell the app was launched from - the app never creates a console window, so killing it cannot close the shell. Killers were still hardened: kill-wysiwyg.ps1 and kill_wysiwyg.bat now also kill whatever LISTENS on 8008/8010 (an elevated process can hide CommandLine from a non-elevated caller) and report failures / warn when a port is still held instead of claiming success. Launch via pythonw main.py or a shortcut for no console.

question: Why did the first CD/45 Front scan rotate the wrong way?
answer: Two bugs: (1) the scanner process does not inherit the app's sys.path, so 'import gemini_pool' failed ('No module named gemini_pool' in wysiscan_debug.log) and the AI orientation stage never ran - _ai_upright_degrees now bootstraps sys.path with dirname(dirname(__file__)) like the other AI endpoints. (2) Without orientation, the levelling picked a winner at the edge of the +-10deg search (logged 11.0 deg) on a booklet-type scan and rotated a good image - edge-of-range winners are now rejected, busy non-text images never rotate, and the failing case now reports 'Already upright.'

question: Why did CD/45 Front look like it crashed the scanner?
answer: Reproduced on the saved scan (ScanGroup_6.jpg, 1240x1753): the code does not crash and correctly answers 90deg, but gemini_pool's timeout is per-attempt and it fails over across models/keys - combo#0 and #1 each timed out (20s each) before a good combo answered, so the scan request hung ~44s and the page's fetch ended in 'TypeError: Failed to fetch'. Fixed: per-attempt timeout 6s, whole AI step capped at 25s wall clock in a worker thread (abandoned on timeout), answers cached per file, straighten can never raise (wrapped at the function and both call sites), and progress/timing lines added to wysiscan_debug.log. Measured 16.6s end-to-end afterwards.

question: What caused the 404 'Nothing matches the given URI' page?
answer: My throwaway python -m http.server test listeners (used to verify the port-owner kill logic) were left running on port 8008. That error page is CPython's http.server default 404, so requests on 8008 hit the test listener instead of the app. Fixed by killing every '*http.server*' python process; 8008 and 8010 are now free. Lesson: never leave test listeners on 8008/8010 - use a port outside the app's range (e.g. 8123) or verify cleanup with Get-NetTCPConnection before finishing.

question: How does CD/45 Front level label text that sits at an arbitrary angle?
answer: The +-10deg row-projection sweep could not reach a label that sits 33deg off, and simply widening it to +-45 failed its own regression harness (the score moves with the white fill a rotation adds, so 12deg was read as 10.75 and 33 as 0, while artwork and radial labels produced 30-43deg false answers). Replaced with a rotation-invariant word-blob method: Otsu, keep elongated non-solid blobs (fill 0.12-0.70 rejects printed blocks and photo highlights), each blob's long axis is its text angle, require >=4 blobs with >=60% within 3deg, then refine +-2deg in 0.25deg on the agreeing blobs only. Measured at 1400px and 800px; if the two disagree by >3deg it is ambiguous and the scan is left alone. Caps: >45deg refused (perpendicular ambiguity), and >15deg refused when the AI gave no orientation (upside-down ambiguity). The old +-10 sweep stays as the fallback. Real failing scan: 34.1deg end-to-end against a truth of 34.0, residual 0.00 after crop; an already-level scan is left byte-identical.

question: How do WysiScan image-adjustment defaults and presets work?
answer: The Image Adjust sliders keep three presets in config.json under adjust_presets: default, custom1, custom2, each holding brightness/contrast/saturation/hue/tint. The page saves the selected slot itself 400ms after a slider stops moving via POST /adjust-preset, so there is no Save button. Only 'default' is applied automatically: apply_default_adjustments() runs after auto-crop in /trigger-scan and /import-file (and after /recrop so Adjust Pad cannot undo it), keeps the pristine copy first so Reset All still works, does nothing when the preset is all zeros, and never raises. Defaults go on the cropped output only, matching the existing rule that the raw scan stays raw. Pressing Apply while the sliders still hold untouched Default values is refused to avoid baking the same values twice. The redundant green Save under the cropped image was removed along with saveCurrentCropped().

question: Why are the Image Adjust buttons labelled Boost and Remove All?
answer: The user renamed them for clarity and asked that they not be changed back: the old Reset button (resetImageAdjustSliders, zeroes the sliders and leaves the image untouched) is now labelled Boost, and the old Reset All button (resetImageAdjustAll, restores the pristine scan) is now labelled Remove All. Only the visible text changed - onclick handlers and the tooltips were left as they were. Do not revert these labels in a future tidy-up.

question: How does the WysiScan tilt control work now?
answer: It is absolute and applies on click instead of relative-plus-Apply. < and > step the angle by 1 degree, << and >> by 10, the number box shows the current angle and typing in it applies too, and Reset returns to 0. A new POST /tilt-image keeps a per-file tilt base copy (TEMP_DIR/<path>.tiltbase) and always restores it before rotating, so 1, 2, 3, 4 degrees each rotate the untouched pixels once - no compounding JPEG loss and no drifting canvas, which is what the old relative flow caused (it posted each delta to /deskew-image and rotated the already-rotated file). One backup is taken when the base is created, so a single Undo returns the pre-tilt scan. The base is only trusted while the file mtime matches what tilt last wrote; any other edit makes the next tilt rebuild the base from disk, and the page resets the displayed angle to 0 when an image refreshes for a non-tilt reason. Requests are chained and setting the same angle twice is byte-identical.

question: How does tilt press-and-hold work in WysiScan?
answer: The four tilt buttons repeat while held: pointerdown applies the first step immediately, then a 350ms delay starts repeating - 1 degree every 110ms for < and >, 10 degrees every 180ms for << and >>. pointerup/pointerleave/pointercancel and window pointerup/blur all stop it so a release outside the button cannot leave it running. Clicks that come from a pointer are ignored in the click handler (event.detail > 0) so a tap steps exactly once, while keyboard activation (detail 0) still steps once. Tilt requests coalesce instead of queueing: one request is in flight at a time, intermediate angles are dropped and the worker re-sends only if the displayed value moved, so holding a button cannot pile up restores and rotations.

question: Why did holding the tilt buttons crash the WysiScan server, and what fixed it?
answer: It was a native crash, not a Python exception: the Windows event log shows pythonw.exe faulting in ntdll.dll with 0xc0000374 (STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION) at the exact moment wysiscan_debug.log stops, after ~10 tilt requests a second (each hold tick sent a request per file, original and cropped). Every request rewrote the same file the browser was re-fetching, so native decodes and writes overlapped on one file. Fixes: the page throttles to at most one tilt request every 400ms plus a final one when the number stops (taps still apply instantly), only one request is ever in flight, the server takes a global _TILT_LOCK so two tilt writes cannot run concurrently, and file writes are atomic (build a temp file, os.replace) so a reader never sees a half-written JPEG. The base is now read directly and written to the destination instead of copying the 6MB base over the file first - 3ms per request on a test image. Re-verified: absolute/idempotent/reset-exact behaviour intact, no temp leftovers, and 24 concurrent requests from 8 threads complete with zero errors and a readable file.

question: What does Remove All do in WysiScan now?
answer: It removes only colour: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue and tint. It no longer restores a pristine snapshot, because that also undid any tilt or rotation made after the colour was applied (the reported bug). Every adjustment is now recorded per file in _ADJUST_HISTORY by /adjust-image and by the Default preset at scan time, and Remove All replays _unadjust_image in reverse order (tint, saturation/hue, brightness, contrast) over the current pixels, so geometry is untouched. Accuracy is 45-48 dB where nothing was clipped and 40.7 dB inside the artwork with a tilt in between; pixels blown out to pure white by a bright adjustment cannot be recovered, and rotation margins can shift about 13 levels because they were filled with white after the adjustment. History is dropped whenever the pixels are replaced (scan, import, recrop, revert-crop, undo, redo, delete) so a stale record can never darken a scan twice, and get_pristine_path plus the .pristine snapshots were removed since nothing restores a whole scan now.

question: How does tilt direction, the rotation crop buffer and the slider reset rules work in WysiScan?
answer: Tilt: > and >> now turn the picture right (clockwise) and < / << turn it left; the page keeps positive = right and negates only when posting, because OpenCV positive is counter-clockwise (verified with a marker blob). Rotation clipping: _rotate_file_by used to re-crop with auto_crop_image, whose contour heuristics latch onto the dark artwork half once the rotated picture fills its own canvas (739x949 with 73 dark pixels shaved off the rim on the real scan). It now uses _content_bbox: compare against the actual border colour, box everything that differs, and add a buffer of 1.5% of the long side (at least the padding). The same scan at -34 now gives 780x850 with zero ink on any edge. Sliders: Apply keeps the values (another Apply stacks on purpose) and Remove All zeroes them; the CSS preview shows only the delta not already baked in, tracked in adjustApplied, and zero sliders clear the filter entirely so nothing is shown twice. A new Reset Default link under the presets zeroes the Default preset and the sliders showing it, posted through the existing /adjust-preset endpoint.

question: Why did the image wobble and shrink while tilting, and how is it fixed?
answer: The first clipping fix cropped the rotated picture to a box of 'everything that differs from the border colour' plus a margin. That is wrong for a real CD crop: the disc is tight enough that it runs off all four edges, so the corner pixels are disc pixels and there is no background to measure. The box therefore jumped every rotation (image appeared to wobble around the white area, crop looked wrong) and the resulting size changed each click (looked like shrinking). _content_bbox was deleted. The shipped approach rotates on an expanded canvas and crops straight back to the original canvas size, centred, via _rotate_file_by(keep_frame=...). A disc is unchanged by rotation, so a 756x737 tight crop stays 756x737 at +5/+14/+30 degrees with zero dark pixels on the rim, and clicking 1,2,3,4,5 in turn never drifts. The page sends media_type: tape/cd keep the frame, lp/auto keep the wider canvas so a rectangular sleeve does not lose its corners.

question: How does tilt interact with the Original and the crop now?
answer: Only the Last Scan (Cropped) image is tilted; the raw Original is never sent to /tilt-image, so it stays exactly as scanned. _rotate_file_by rotates the cropped base onto a canvas expanded by the angle plus a 4% background margin, then crops that rotated picture itself - never the original bed scan, which is what Adjust Pad does and why it lost the tilt. For discs (tape/cd) _disc_crop fits a circle to the background-difference mask and crops a centred square of 2r + 2*padding, giving 746-747 px at every angle from 1 to 30 degrees (1 px spread, always square, zero rim ink) versus 735-759 with the contour crop. LP/Auto go through the normal auto_crop_image on the rotated picture, safe now that the margin exists. An implausible circle fit falls back to the contour crop, and auto_crop_image is given a separate temp path because it raises SameFileError when writing over its own input with no contours found.

question: How does Remove All restore the untouched colour-free image?
answer: Instead of undoing the adjustment maths (which cannot recover highlights clipped to white by a bright adjustment), the server now keeps a copy of the real pixels in TEMP/<path>.plain, taken just before the first adjustment lands - both the Default preset at scan time and every Apply. Remove All swaps that copy back, so with no geometry change the file is byte-identical to the pre-colour original (verified by SHA, including after two stacked Applies). If a tilt happened after the colour, the tilt is replayed on the restored copy using the crop window stored by the tilt itself (_TILT_STATE[key].crop_rect), giving identical framing (727x727 before and after, bit-identical to rotating the colour-free pixels with the same window). A geometry generation counter, bumped by rotate-image, rotate-image-fine, deskew-image, auto-deskew, manual-crop and manual-crop-replace, decides whether the snapshot is still trustworthy; recrop, revert-crop, undo, redo, scan, import and delete drop it outright. When it is not trustworthy Remove All falls back to undoing the maths so colour still comes off.

question: How is the Box Sleeve Condition column wired?
answer: Sleeve (All Types) gained a fourth column, BOX SLEEVE CONDITION, backed by a new boxSleeve array in Conditions.json (currently empty; the user will fill it later). It follows the same pattern as the other sleeve types: options are rendered into sleeveConditionOptions with data-media-type=boxSleeve and are always hidden in the normal per-type multiselect, selections live in a new hidden select #boxSleeveOptions, syncConditionMultiselectsToLegacy distributes them, and customOptionsSelected now includes them so they flow into the description once the list is populated. editor.html gained a Box Sleeve Conditions section in the conditions editor (add/edit/delete/search/save) and the four sections wrap with flex-wrap instead of squeezing. The in-app Edit Conditions modal still covers only Media/Sleeve for LP/CD/Cassette; editing the box list is done in editor.html as requested. Conditions.json was rewritten with the app's own json.dump(indent=4) formatting so the diff is only the pending edits plus the new key.

question: How does the sleeve condition list switch for box sets?
answer: When Sleeve Packaging has a value matching /box\s*set/i (Box Set or Boxset), the Sleeve Condition multiselect shows customOptionsData.boxSleeve and hides LP/CD/Cassette. isBoxSetSelected() reads the packaging multiselect and effectiveSleeveType() returns boxSleeve or the current media type; renderConditionMultiselects() filters visibility on that. Triggers: after the scrape fills packaging, the packaging select's change event, the packaging list-picker Done/Close/Clear handlers, and fullReset() so Reset All restores the media-type list. The Open Sleeve (Current Type) button and its context-menu entry open the Box Set list while Box Set is selected and the picker header reads BOX SET SLEEVE CONDITION. Favouriting a multiselect selection now resolves each row's own data-media-type instead of assuming the current media type. Hidden LP/CD/Cassette selections are kept, not cleared.

question: How does the Both view and Edit Conditions handle Box Set?
answer: In the dual (Both) condition picker the media column now takes its type from the on-screen Media Type dropdown rather than the caller's argument, so it no longer drifts to a default, and the sleeve column uses effectiveSleeveType() - with Box Set selected it lists the Box Sleeve conditions and the header reads BOX SET SLEEVE CONDITION; toggling and the row favourite menu use the same type. The Edit Conditions modal gained Box Set in both of its media type dropdowns (the filter and the new-entry one) so customOptionsData.boxSleeve can be listed, added, edited, favourited and deleted like any other sleeve list; while Box Set is selected the modal forces the Sleeve Condition category and hides Media Condition, rows tag themselves [BOX SET], and opening Edit List from the sleeve multiselect lands on Box Set (the plain Edit button clears that sticky choice so it follows the form again).

question: How is the editor Colours window built?
answer: editor.html gained a purple (6f42c1) Colours button between Conditions and Exit Editor. It opens a full-screen modal like Manage Conditions but with two columns, Colour and Texture, each a list of single-value rows (text input plus delete) with an + Add New button; entries are plain strings, not title/text pairs. The window reads GET /api/colourmap and writes POST /api/save-colourmap (Save) or POST /api/admin/sync-colourmap (Upload To Server, which backs up the master and writes the share copy only, mirroring sync-conditions). Data lives in colourmap.json at the program root as {colour: [], texture: []}; main.py serves a DEFAULT_COLOURMAP when the file is missing and resolves the server path through get_server_colourmap_path (server_dir/colourmap.json). Not yet packaged: colourmap.json still needs adding to !build.bat/WYSIWYG.spec and the .iss before it ships with an install.

question: What are the Colour and TextMod columns and their data?
answer: The Colours window in editor.html now has two columns: Colour and TextMod (the second was originally called Texture). colourmap.json stores them as {colour: [...], textmod: [...]} and the reader still accepts a legacy 'texture' key. Populated from the user's supplied master lists: 98 colours (Gold, Gold / Golden, Silver ... Indigo, including effect words like Clear/Translucent/Crystal/Neon which the user classes as Colours) and 46 text mods (Splatter, Marble, Marbled, Swirl ... Stained Glass). Merge rule: keep the supplied order, drop case-insensitive duplicates, and never let a name sit in both columns - overlaps are removed from TextMod. Result 98 + 46 = 144 entries, zero duplicates.

question: Why roll .continuity/SESSION_NOTES.md forward to 1.20.15.0?
answer: The notes still described the 2026-07/2026-10 Walmart-Exporter era and 1.15.3.18, five versions behind. They now reflect 1.20.15.0 (2026-11-16 release), the current artefacts, the restart/rebuild gotchas, and a pointer to docs/WORK_LOG.md for history. Prior sections remain in git history.

question: Why does the refresh Reset All no longer use the 3 s fallback?
answer: The load listener and 3 s backstop were registered after awaiting /settings, so a slow settings fetch missed an already-fired load event and the previous item's menus stayed on screen until the timer ran. The settings promise now starts first, the hooks are registered immediately, the reset awaits that promise itself, readyState=complete runs on the next tick, and the backstop is 1500 ms. The remaining delay is the parser-blocking htmx CDN script; Scott chose not to vendor it for now.

question: Why do the condition multiselects keep their scroll position now?
answer: Clicking a row in the inline Media/Sleeve Condition listboxes made Chrome scroll the listbox to its active option, which the mousedown preventDefault did not stop; the handler now records scrollTop and restores it on the next frame. renderConditionMultiselects also rebuilds both lists with innerHTML='' and reset the scroll on every re-render, so renderSelect now saves and restores scrollTop per list. Modal pickers already preserved scroll.

question: Why did the heartbeat watchdog kill the app on a coworker's machine?
answer: LAST_HEARTBEAT is set at import and the watchdog exited once now-LAST_HEARTBEAT > 12s, but the first heartbeat cannot arrive until the page parses past the parser-blocking unpkg htmx scripts. A cold machine missed the window and the process terminated itself, which looks like a crash (tab shows connection refused). The same 12s killed the server after a slow reload (pagehide pops the tab) and after laptop sleep/resume (stale tab pruned, exit check raced the next 3s ping). Now nothing is killed until a tab has registered once (60s startup allowance), no-tab grace is 30s, hidden tabs last 4h, and a prune counts as activity so a waking machine can re-register.

question: Why was the Adds submenu replaced by a top-level Amazon Adds button?
answer: Scott asked for Amazon to move up one level and be renamed Amazon Adds, with the Adds menu item removed - a submenu whose only visible entry was Amazon cost a click for nothing. Adds and addsToggleBtn markup, toggleAddsSubmenu, its close-drawer exception and the addsDiscogsBtn wiring were removed. Discogs Adds stays reachable via its Ctrl+Shift+D hotkey. The drawer-submenu CSS is left in place, and the 2026-10-12 decision to keep the hidden Discogs button for restore is superseded.

question: Why was the Discogs Adds hotkey removed?
answer: Scott asked for it to be removed 'for now' because the feature is a long way from working. discogsAdds was dropped from HOTKEY_ACTIONS and HOTKEY_DEFAULTS so it no longer shows in Hot Keys and cannot be bound; openAddsDiscogs() and the /adds/discogs route are left intact so it can be re-added when the feature works. A stale discogsAdds binding may remain in localStorage but nothing reads it.

question: Why is Discogs Adds stripped from the build and installer?
answer: The feature is a long way from working and is no longer reachable (menu entry, button and hotkey removed), so Scott asked for it out of the build. build.bat deletes the Discogs files from dist\WYSIWYG\_internal\Adds after PyInstaller, and the ISS excludes the same paths plus an [InstallDelete] section that removes them from older installs on upgrade. Source files stay in Adds\; the /adds/discogs route and its prompt file are left in place, unreachable.

question: Why was this release built as 1.20.16.0 with its own changelog section?
answer: The app's update check (/api/server-version) only reports update_available when the server's version.json is strictly greater than the bundled copy, so rebuilding at 1.20.15.0 would install but never prompt any machine. version.json and MyAppVersion are now 1.20.16.0, and this batch's six fixes sit under a new v1.20.16.0 - 2026-11-17 heading instead of being appended to the already-shipped 1.20.15.0 section. Nothing was copied to the FYRShare folder yet.

question: Why do close_local_chrome.ps1 and version.json ship in dist_install?
answer: run_me_Installer.bat only closes the app's browser windows when close_local_chrome.ps1 sits next to it, and the update check reads version.json from the publish folder (\\\\192.168.0.108\\FYRShare\\Tools\\FYRTools\\WYSIWYG), so both now get copied into dist_install by !build.bat alongside run_me_Installer.bat before ISCC runs. A stale version.json there means no machine ever sees the update banner.

question: How is the WysiScanStandalone desktop build done?
answer: Windowed only in WysiScanStandalone: scanner_server.py defaults to a pywebview/WebView2 window around the same 127.0.0.1:8010 server (--browser keeps the tab, --launched-by-main unchanged), and build_windowed.py produces a PyInstaller onedir windowed build in dist_windowed. Chosen over QtWebEngine to keep the download sane and because pywebview+pythonnet are already installed; onedir instead of onefile so WebView2 starts fast and Defender sees the same shape as WYSIWYG. Nothing in WysiScan/, the embedded scanner or the installer changed.

question: Why does the test scanner run on 8011 and read version.json?
answer: Scott wants the WysiScanStandalone test build usable on the same machine as the real scanner, so every 8010 reference in that copy (uvicorn bind, window/browser URLs, CORS origins, the page's API_BASE) is now 8011. version.json (2.5.0.66) ships in the bundle and next to the exe, is logged at startup, shown in the window title and served at GET /api/version. Browse dialogs needed --collect-submodules=tkinter because only the tkinter package was collected and tkinter.filedialog was missing at runtime.

question: Why is the standalone test scanner called XenoScan?
answer: Scott renamed the WysiScanStandalone test build to XenoScan (exe, dist folder, window title, HTML title, logs, spec), while the shipped WysiScan\ build inside WYSIWYG stays WysiScan. The folder is now tracked as its own git repo at C:\Git\WysiWyg-Browser\WysiScanStandalone. Internal identifiers (ASSET_DIR 'WysiScan', log filename, JS function names, icon files) were deliberately left alone because they are paths/ids, not user-facing names.

question: How are the XenoScan icon and shared Xeno_ui used?
answer: XenoScan.ico is generated from the supplied square artwork (centre crop, 16-256 multi-size) and is both the exe icon and the page favicon; XenoScan.png is the artwork image. The window shell uses C:\\Git\\Xeno_ui: theme.BG_COLOR as the webview background, menus.py for the native File/Help menu bar (Open Files drives the page import button, Open Folder opens scans, About shows a second window from about.py). The page keeps its own blue/yellow palette - the Xeno_ui accent is shell-only unless Scott asks for a page restyle.

question: Why does XenoScan keep its own keys and open Extract Text in-app?
answer: Inside the pywebview shell window.open() is handed to the system browser, so Extract Text opened as a tab; the window now exposes a JS API (_ShellApi.open_extract) and the page calls it, falling back to window.open for browser mode. Keys: _load_main_env_file now reads only APP_DIR\\.env, and gemini_pool gained an opt-in XENO_KEY_DIR that the scanner sets to its own folder, so the test build can never borrow the main app's keys. The gemini_pool change is additive - WYSIWYG sets no such variable.

question: What palette does XenoScan use now and where is its menu?
answer: XenoScan's colours come from the Image Convert app: near-black #060608 base, #121218 panels, slate text, cyan #06b6d4 primary, violet #a855f7 secondary, green/amber/red accents. The stylesheet and the inline style attributes were remapped from the old blue/yellow Bootstrap palette, and the app now starts in dark mode unless light was chosen last time. The in-page Menu drawer is replaced by a native menu bar: File (open files/folder, exit), Options (toggle theme, hot keys) and Help (About) - File and Help from Xeno_ui.menus, Options built with webview.menu. The drawer button is hidden only inside the desktop shell.

question: Why is XenoScan's layout fluid instead of a 1200px card?
answer: Scott's screenshot showed the scanner sitting in a centred 1200px card with wide gutters and the page background showing around it, which reads as a web page inside a window frame. A DESKTOP WORKSPACE block (scoped to body:not(.extract-mode)) now makes the container full-width/min-height 100vh with no radius or shadow, turns the two top panels and the control strip into Image Convert-style cards, and raises the compact block's 11px type back to 12-13px. The Extract Text window keeps its own layout.

question: Why should multi-medium releases rebuild the media string instead of only Box Set releases?
answer: The rebuild from the formats array was gated on a Discogs 'Box Set' format entry, but release 10070875 (Pink Floyd - The Early Years 1970) has plain 2xCD / 2xDVD / Blu-ray entries, so it collapsed to a single medium and lost the CDs and Blu-ray. Gate widened to needsFormatsMedia() = has Box Set entry OR more than one distinct medium name (All Media/Box Set ignored). Repeated entries of the same medium still use the old single-medium path, so existing output is unchanged.

question: How should small WYSIWYG fixes ship without a full reinstall?
answer: Loose-file patch channel in patches\\. make_patch.bat builds a folder from a whitelist of runtime files that resource_path() reads from the install dir (app.js, index.html, styles.css, data.json, colourmap.json, changelog.txt, ChromeExt...), writes patch.json with SHA-256 per file, and optionally publishes to <share>\\WYSIWYG\\patches\\<version>\\. apply_patch.bat stops the app, backs up replaced files to C:\\FYRTOOLS\\wysiwyg.patch-backup, copies version.json last, verifies hashes and rolls back on mismatch. Conditions.json, .env and keys are never patchable; any changed .py or bundled code aborts the build so Python fixes cannot be shipped as a JS-only patch.

question: Why does the patch tooling have a Tk GUI in patches\\?
answer: Scott found the README-only workflow hard to follow. patches\\Patch GUI.bat opens a tkinter window (project dark palette, no new dependency, not shipped) with three tabs: build (tick changed files, note, optional publish, bump version), apply (dry run / apply with backup+verify), and a plain-English rules tab. The GUI calls the same make_patch.ps1/apply_patch.ps1 scripts; make_patch.ps1 gained -List so the whitelist lives in one place. Version bump updates version.json, the .iss MyAppVersion and the changelog heading in one confirmed step, preserving each file's line endings.

question: How do published patches reach client machines without manual installs?
answer: The app advertises them. main.py list_server_patches() reads <share>\\WYSIWYG\\patches\\*\\patch.json; /api/server-version returns either patch_available (newest patch >= installer) or update_available (strictly newer installer), never both. app.js shows 'PATCH x.y.z AVAILABLE' in the banner/title and POSTs /run-patch, which launches the patch's apply_patch.ps1 detached so it closes, copies, verifies, rolls back on failure and restarts. Re-checked on visibilitychange. Bootstrap: because the check lives in main.py, the first release carrying it must be a full installer (1.20.19.0); after that JS/HTML/CSS/data fixes ship as patches.

question: Why did the first app-triggered patch close the app and do nothing, and how is it prevented?
answer: The updater is a child of the app, and the old order was backup -> kill the app -> copy, so the kill ended the updater before it copied anything and nobody restarted. apply_patch.ps1 now copies and verifies while the app is still running, then starts a fresh instance which replaces the old one (WYSIWYG already terminates an old instance on startup) - it never kills its own parent. Visibility added: %TEMP%\\wysiwyg_patch_apply.log written at every step, a titled batch window that pauses on failure, and a live Patching screen in app.js that polls /api/version and reloads on the new version.

question: Why not use close_local_chrome.ps1 to avoid duplicate tabs after a patch?
answer: It closes the whole browser window whose caption starts with WYSIWYG (Chrome cannot close one tab externally), taking unrelated tabs with it - fine before an installer, too blunt for a routine patch. Instead the patch no longer restarts the app at all: apply_patch.ps1 skips Start-Process when WYSIWYG was already running, because every patchable file is read from disk per request. The patching page reloads when /api/version reports the target twice (version.json is copied last), so no second tab and no downtime. A closed app is still started.
